candidates.title: Beyond 4 bits: Data-Centric Post-training Quantization and Recovery
candidates.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) compresses the weights of a trained model with a limited compute and data budget. Down to 4 bits, state-of-the-art PTQ methods are near-lossless; below this limit, the tested scalar PTQ configurations collapse to near-random accuracy and quality becomes acutely sensitive to choices such as the quantization representation and calibration data. At such low bitwidths, recovery fine-tuning becomes crucial, and its effectiveness depends heavily on these same choices. Yet there is little systematic evidence on how the quantization method, the quality and task alignment of calibration data, and the design of the recovery procedure interact to determine the final 2-bit model. We present a systematic study of 2-bit quantization and recovery fine-tuning across model families, scales, and data distributions, and distill our findings into practical, architecture-dependent best practices for obtaining an accurate 2-bit model. This recipe, which combines a vector codebook representation, a small task-aligned calibration mixture, and a short codebook-only distillation stage, restores 63-68% average accuracy across seven question-answering tasks at 2 bits (a 71-73% BF16 ceiling), versus the near-random 29% of the evaluated scalar PTQ pipelines, at roughly half the compute of a full-model QAT baseline. Given the same calibration and recovery data, EfficientQAT, a trained scalar baseline, avoids the collapse. However, at a matched rate it trails the vector recipe on generation on every model (2.8-10.9 AvgGen; within noise on Qwen3-MoE) and on question answering on three of the four studied models (2.7-7.8 AvgQA). We also find that the best recovery data depends on the calibration data, an interaction confirmed on a held-out model. Our architecture-aware map of the 2-bit design space shows that representation, calibration data, and recovery data must be chosen jointly.
candidates.reason: Systematic study of 2-bit post-training quantization and recovery fine-tuning across model families that distills a practical recipe (vector codebook representation, task-aligned calibration mixture, codebook-only distillation) for accurate sub-4-bit LLM deployment.

candidates.title: InAttention: Linear Context Scaling for Transformers
candidates.abstract: VRAM requirements for transformer models scale quadratically with context length due to the self-attention mechanism. In this paper we modify the decoder-only transformer, replacing self-attention with InAttention, which scales linearly with context length during inference by having tokens attend only to initial states. Benchmarking shows that InAttention significantly reduces VRAM usage during inference, enabling handling of long sequences on consumer GPUs. We corroborate that fine-tuning extends context length efficiently, improving performance on long sequences without high training costs. InAttention offers a scalable solution for long-range dependencies in transformer models, paving the way for further optimization.
candidates.reason: InAttention replaces decoder self-attention so tokens attend only to initial states, making VRAM scale linearly with context length during inference and enabling long sequences on consumer GPUs.
